continuity_scope: John Boorman's 1981 English-language feature film, the 140-minute Orion Pictures release distributed through Warner Bros., released 10 April 1981. This pass uses AFI's onscreen-prologue record and its opening-to-accession synopsis: divided England through Arthur's drawing Excalibur, parentage disclosure, the siege at Leondegrance's castle, and Uryens's knighting/allegiance. It does not add the later Lancelot/Grail/Mordred material, and does not merge Thomas Malory, other Arthurian texts, novelizations, other films, later remakes, or production alternatives.
work_or_witnesses: Excalibur (1981), John Boorman feature film, 140-minute Orion/Warner theatrical release
AFI Catalog record 56592: film header/details, screen prologue, cast credits, and synopsis paragraphs 1093–1103
coverage_rule: Include every individually named acting character in AFI's selected opening-to-accession segment: Merlin, Uther Pendragon, Cornwall, Igrayne, Morgana, Arthur Pendragon, Kay, Leondegrance, Guenevere, Uryens/Uryen, and the individual titled Lady of the Lake. Excalibur, the sword-in-stone rule, the kingdom/land, castle, knight/squire offices, magic, the truce, and holy/sacred framing are terms or dimensions. Actors are never character nodes. Later named figures (including Lancelot, Perceval, Gawain, Mordred, and others) are out of scope even where AFI credits them.
omissions: All named characters/events occurring after Uryens's knighting/allegiance in the selected synopsis, including the later court, Lancelot, Grail, infidelity, Morgana's later magic, Mordred, illness/disability, war, deaths, nunnery, and final battle.

All detail not stated in AFI's selected synopsis: dialogue, exact film timestamps, full magic rules, artifacts beyond Excalibur, Round Table procedure, named peoples, places beyond England/Leondegrance's castle, religious ritual, and outcomes.

Malory's Le Morte Darthur and all other Arthurian textual witnesses, novelizations, 1950s/1960s/other films, later derivative works, unscreened scripts, fan wikis, Wikipedia, commercial character databases, reviews, and performer biography.
uncertainties: AFI reports that Pallenberg received an onscreen adaptation credit for Malory, but that production fact is not permission to import any Malory-only attribute; every record is solely for this film's AFI-summarized continuity.
AFI says filmmakers deliberately selected an indeterminate medieval time and historical inaccuracy. England and the Dark Ages are the film's fiction framing, not a historical reconstruction.

The synopsis directly describes Uther obtaining sex with Igrayne through Merlin's disguise spell. This record labels it non-consensual sexual deception without graphic detail; it does not call the relationship romantic. Morgana is called Igrayne's young daughter but receives no age, so she is not assigned a numerical age.

The selected segment has military fighting, Cornwall's death, Uther's fatal ambush, and infant removal. They are recorded only at non-graphic premise level. Christianity, sacred kingship, Grail, later disability, and later violence are outside this pass; no real religious claim is made.
evidence_basis: AFI Catalog authoritative film record only, using claim-specific onscreen/prologue, credit, release-detail, and selected-synopsis locators. It establishes this film's distinct release/continuity and selected character events without consulting fan sources or folding in its literary source tradition.
